Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates a widened superior mediastinum and an abnormal bulge of the left cardiac contour, which are classic radiographic signs of traumatic injury to the great vessels, such as rupture of the ascending aorta or pulmonary trunk, rather than isolated ventricular laceration or simple pneumothorax. The "translucent line" likely represents the interface of a mediastinal hematoma or pseudoaneurysm displacing adjacent structures.
